distractorNotes.d: Clearing focus causes the browser to reset focus to the document root, disrupting interaction.

sourceNote: W3C WAI-ARIA 1.2 §6.6 aria-activedescendant maintains focus on container while referencing active child ID.

stem: Why does WAI-ARIA strictly prohibit placing aria-hidden='true' on an element that is focusable or contains focusable descendants?

options.text: It causes web browsers to automatically remove the target element from the sequential keyboard Tab order.
It causes the element to become visually hidden like CSS display: none across all desktop web browsers.
It creates a focus trap for screen reader users where focus lands on controls invisible to screen readers.
It converts focusable interactive controls into unselectable static text nodes in the accessibility tree.

explanation: Applying aria-hidden='true' to a focusable element or a container with focusable children creates an 'accessibility black hole'. A sighted keyboard user or screen reader user tabbing through the page lands on the control, but the screen reader announces nothing because it is hidden in the accessibility tree.

distractorNotes.a: aria-hidden does not alter keyboard focusability; focusable elements still receive Tab focus despite being hidden from screen readers.
distractorNotes.b: aria-hidden affects only the accessibility tree and has no effect on visual rendering or CSS visibility.
distractorNotes.d: aria-hidden removes elements from the accessibility tree entirely rather than converting them into static text.

sourceNote: W3C WAI-ARIA 1.2 §6.6 aria-hidden specifies focusable elements must never have aria-hidden true.

stem: Which HTML5 semantic element automatically provides the ARIA landmark role 'main' when placed within the document body?

options.text: <article>
options.hintText: represents a self-contained composition such as a forum post or news item

options.text: <section>
options.hintText: represents a generic standalone section of a document without an inherent landmark role

options.text: <div>
options.hintText: represents a generic flow container without default semantic meaning

options.text: <main>
options.hintText: represents the dominant or central content of the document body

explanation: The main element natively exposes the ARIA main landmark role without requiring role='main'. It represents the dominant content of the body of a document or application.

distractorNotes.a: The article element maps to the ARIA article role, which is a structural role rather than a landmark role.
distractorNotes.b: An unnamed section element does not expose a landmark role (it only becomes a region landmark when labelled).
distractorNotes.c: A div with a CSS class has no semantic role in the accessibility tree.

sourceNote: HTML specification §4.4.14 defines main element mapping to the ARIA main landmark role.

stem: An HTML input element has both an associated label element and a title attribute. Which source is used for its accessible name?

options.text: The associated label element
options.hintText: host-language labeling element associated with the input control

options.text: The title attribute
options.hintText: advisory attribute commonly presented as a browser tooltip

options.text: Both sources concatenated
options.hintText: joins multiple naming sources separated by whitespace

options.text: The title attribute overriding label
options.hintText: advisory tooltip text superseding the semantic label element

explanation: Under the Accessible Name and Description Computation (AccName 1.2), native host language markup (such as `<label for="...">`) has higher precedence than fallback attributes like title or placeholder. The title attribute is only used as an accessible name if no label or ARIA labeling attribute exists.

distractorNotes.b: The title attribute is a fallback attribute evaluated only if no higher-precedence labeling mechanism is present.
distractorNotes.c: The algorithm selects the higher-priority name source rather than combining them into a compound string.
distractorNotes.d: In AccName 1.2, native label elements have higher precedence than title attributes, which serve only as fallbacks.

sourceNote: W3C AccName 1.2 §4.3 Step 2D defines native label element precedence over title attribute fallback.

stem: How does role='status' differ from role='alert' in how assistive technology handles dynamic updates?

options.text: role='status' requires aria-atomic='true' declared manually, while role='alert' defaults to polite live.
role='status' provides an implicit polite live region waiting for idle, while role='alert' interrupts speech.
role='status' announces updates only when focused, while role='alert' speaks updates when unfocused.
role='status' requires an explicit user keypress to announce, while role='alert' announces upon mouse hover.

explanation: The role status has implicit aria-live='polite' and aria-atomic='true', meaning updates are spoken at the next available pause without interrupting the user. The role alert has implicit aria-live='assertive' and aria-atomic='true', causing screen readers to interrupt ongoing speech immediately.

distractorNotes.a: Both role='status' and role='alert' have implicit aria-atomic='true' by default under the WAI-ARIA specification.
distractorNotes.c: Both live roles announce dynamic updates without requiring keyboard focus to be placed on the container.
distractorNotes.d: Neither role requires explicit user keypresses or mouse hovers to trigger announcements; they announce on DOM updates.

sourceNote: W3C WAI-ARIA 1.2 §5.4 defines role status as polite and role alert as assertive.

stem: When a web page contains an image that functions as a link to the organization homepage, what should its alt attribute contain?

options.text: A detailed visual description of the organization logo color scheme and pixel dimensions.
An empty string (alt='') to ensure screen readers skip past the hyperlink entirely.
A concise description of the link destination, such as the organization name and homepage indicator.
The word 'link' followed by the full raw destination URL string.

explanation: When an image is the sole content of a link, its alternative text must convey the purpose or destination of the link (e.g. 'Acme Home') rather than visual appearance. Setting alt='' creates an unlabelled link, which severely impedes screen reader navigation.

distractorNotes.a: Visual descriptions of colors or dimensions fail to communicate the functional destination of the link.
distractorNotes.b: Setting alt='' on a linked image creates an empty link that screen readers announce as an unlabelled link or raw URL.
distractorNotes.d: Screen readers already announce the element as a link, so including 'link' is redundant, and raw URLs are verbose.

sourceNote: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content requires linked images to describe link destination or purpose.

stem: According to the W3C WAI 'Using ARIA' guidelines, what restriction applies to the use of the aria-roledescription attribute?

options.text: It can be applied to any generic div or span without specifying an underlying concrete ARIA role.
It can only be used on elements with role='presentation' to convert decorative elements to controls.
It automatically creates custom operating system keyboard shortcuts matching the description text.
It must only be used on elements with an ARIA role, and should not override standard roles unnecessarily.

explanation: aria-roledescription defines a human-readable, localized description of an element's role. It must only be applied to elements that already have a defined ARIA role. Using it arbitrarily or overriding standard roles (like 'button' or 'link') confuses users by replacing familiar assistive technology role announcements.

distractorNotes.a: aria-roledescription must only be used on elements that already possess an implicit or explicit ARIA role.
distractorNotes.b: Applying aria-roledescription to role='presentation' is an antipattern because presentation suppresses semantic roles.
distractorNotes.c: aria-roledescription is a text label for assistive technology announcements and does not create keyboard shortcuts.

sourceNote: W3C WAI-ARIA 1.2 §6.6 aria-roledescription specifies use only on elements with concrete roles.
